transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~8 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Aurora - Security Lead), Claire O'Neill (Aurora - Eng Mgr), Maya Ruiz (Aurora - Compliance)

Summary:
- Review of recent 3rd-party pen test findings (redwood-hosted deployment in eu-west-1)
- Discuss remediation timelines, vuln triage, patching cadence and re-test plan
- Cover RBAC/SSO questions, audit log retention and KMS/BYOK options

Topics: SOC2 status, pen test findings (critical/medium/low), vuln management process, secure SDLC practices (SAST/DAST/dependency scanning), patching windows, RBAC/SCIM/SAML, audit logs retention, encryption & KMS, data residency and re-test cadence.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call, then we'll jump into the pen test results. we sent the executive summary last night, full report attached in the calendar invite.
[00:07] Samir Patel: yep, got that. thanks Jordan. before we start, high level from our side: we need to understand severity, expected remediation timelines, and proof we'll get for compliance.
[00:15] Jordan Lee: absolutely. Priya's going to run through the findings and suggested remediation steps, and then we can align on timelines.
[00:20] Priya Nair: hi all. quick context: test scope was our hosted offering in eu-west-1, customer-data plane only, pen tester noted list of issues - one critical, several medium, a handful of low/infos. I'll go issue-by-issue.
[00:32] Priya Nair: Critical: JWT token refresh endpoint had an edge case where expired tokens could be accepted if clock skew plus certain refresh flow - that was flagged as a session fixation/logic bug. we reproduced it, it's real but only in a narrow flow. mitigation: tighten clock validation and canonicalize refresh path, add additional checks server-side. we propose patch within 72 hours for criticals.
[00:55] Claire O'Neill: can you say whether that affects dedicated or private customers? we run dedicated pools for some regs.
[01:02] Priya Nair: good question - the vulnerable flow is in the hosted token broker service that handles short-lived tokens for the hosted api. Dedicated/private deployments using their own token brokers aren't affected unless they pull the same broker image and config; for private on-prem we provide a patched image.
[01:16] Samir Patel: ok that's helpful. we need E2E evidence of the fix. will you provide tests?
[01:21] Priya Nair: yes - unit/regression tests plus a verification test plan. we'll provide test artifacts and a re-run of the specific exploit.
[01:28] Priya Nair: Medium: debug endpoints left enabled in a staging cluster that leaked internal service metadata. low impact on customer PII but can aid reconnaissance. remediation: disable debug endpoints by default, add feature flag gated by environment; also add automated scans to CI to detect exposed endpoints.
[01:45] Jordan Lee: on the CI point - our secure SDLC includes SAST and dependency scanning; we will extend DAST to test for exposed debug routes in pre-prod.
[01:52] Maya Ruiz: what about dependency vulnerabilities - do you run SBOM and CVE scans? we need to show auditors.
[01:58] Priya Nair: yes, SBOM generated for every build, we run dependency scanning with vuln ratings, and there's a triage workflow. high/critical are blocked from promotion until triaged.
[02:07] Samir Patel: what are your SLA/cadence targets for patching? we need concrete numbers for our internal policy.
[02:12] Jordan Lee: our current target is: critical within 72 hours of identification, high within 2 weeks, medium within 30 days, and generic monthly maintenance window for routine patches. we also run emergency hotfixes outside the window for criticals.
[02:25] Claire O'Neill: 30 days for medium is ok but we also need visibility into backlog and remediation tickets.
[02:30] Jordan Lee: we'll provide a remediation tracker that maps each finding to an internal ticket and owner - you'll get that with the full report.
[02:37] Samir Patel: regarding audit/logging - how long do you retain request-level logs and who can access them? we need 12 months for our compliance.
[02:46] Priya Nair: by default we retain API audit logs for 90 days in hosted, with an enterprise add-on for 12-24 month retention. access is RBAC controlled; only designated ops/security roles have access. for dedicated/private you can set retention policy locally.
[02:58] Maya Ruiz: and are logs tamper-evident / do you provide integrity hashes or export to customer-managed KMS?
[03:04] Priya Nair: logs are write-once in the storage tier and we support exporting logs to customer-owned AWS accounts via cross-account delivery; we can sign logs with KMS-backed signing keys if needed.
[03:12] Samir Patel: KMS - we heard you support BYOK?
[03:15] Jordan Lee: yes, bring-your-own-key via AWS KMS is supported for encryption-at-rest for customer data; for private on-prem we support HSM integration. we can show the KMS integration doc.
[03:23] Claire O'Neill: encryption in transit? TLS 1.3 across all endpoints?
[03:27] Priya Nair: TLS 1.3 by default, server cipher suites hardened, mutual TLS optional for private endpoints.
[03:33] Samir Patel: back to remediation: how will you prove the medium issues are gone - is it just code diff or will you allow us to run a limited verification/pen test?
[03:42] Jordan Lee: we typically run a focused re-test for criticals and high items. for medium items we provide remediation evidence and the pen tester can be re-engaged at customer request; we'll coordinate a scoped re-test.
[03:52] Priya Nair: timeboxes: critical re-test in ~2 weeks; high items we aim to close and verify in 4 weeks where feasible.
[03:59] Maya Ruiz: does Redwood have SOC2? we need SOC2 Type II evidence as part of our vendor review.
[04:05] Jordan Lee: Redwood is currently SOC2 in progress, Type II targeted Q2 2026; we can share our interim controls and gap remediation plan. we do have ISO 27001 assessment planned later this year.
[04:16] Samir Patel: we will need an evidence bundle - policies, org chart, control owners.
[04:20] Jordan Lee: understood, Maya - we'll package a SOC2 artifacts bundle and redacted reports where applicable.
[04:24] Priya Nair: a few operational notes: RBAC supports role templates, and we have SCIM provisioning for groups in SSO. SAML SSO is supported for enterprise tenants and we can enforce SCIM-provisioned group sync so you can centrally control who has admin/operator access.
[04:40] Claire O'Neill: does SCIM send group membership updates in near real-time? we want to ensure offboarding is immediate.
[04:45] Priya Nair: syncs are near-real-time (usually under a minute) for most IdPs; we also have push events and there's a manual revoke API for emergency offboard.
[04:54] Samir Patel: audit logs for admin activity - can we restrict to only admins and compliance team?
[04:59] Jordan Lee: yes, RBAC + audit configuration allows you to limit access; logs still record actions but are encrypted and access controlled.
[05:06] Claire O'Neill: any third-party dependencies that were flagged in the pen test?
[05:10] Priya Nair: a small set of outdated packages were flagged, most low/medium. dependency scanning is in place and we'll bump versions as part of the remediation.
[05:18] Jordan Lee: another point - our deployment pipeline is immutable images, SBOM attached, and every change goes through SAST/DAST and manual security gate for high-risk components.
[05:28] Maya Ruiz: what's your vulnerability disclosure and bug bounty posture?
[05:31] Priya Nair: we have a coordinated vulnerability disclosure process and a limited private bug bounty program for qualified researchers. we'll share the policy.
[05:38] Samir Patel: ok good. on patching cadence, one ask: can we get a monthly patch schedule and a notification window?
[05:44] Jordan Lee: yes, you'll be on the enterprise maintenance calendar; notifications go out 7 days and 24 hours prior to maintenance, and emergency windows outside of that for critical fixes.
[05:52] Claire O'Neill: for dedicated customers, do you provide an option to apply patches ourselves? some customers want control.
[05:58] Priya Nair: for dedicated we provide images and an orchestrated upgrade plan; we can support self-managed patching in private deployments with support contract.
[06:06] Samir Patel: can we get a single-line summary of the critical and top 3 medium items for our board?
[06:10] Jordan Lee: yes - critical: JWT refresh flow fix being deployed; top mediums: exposed debug endpoint, dependency CVEs (low/medium), and insufficient rate-limiting on certain admin APIs. we'll include a one-pager.
[06:22] Priya Nair: quick ops-technical note on admin APIs - we can add a default rate-limit and stricter RBAC on admin routes as a short-term mitigation.
[06:29] Samir Patel: that would be good.
[06:31] Jordan Lee: action plan recap: we'll send the full pen test PDF and remediation tracker by tomorrow, Priya will share SCIM/SAML docs and a test account, you'll have the remediation tracker mapping each finding to a ticket and owner. re-test planning targeted in two weeks for criticals.
[06:46] Maya Ruiz: and SOC2 evidence?
[06:48] Jordan Lee: yes, we'll share the SOC2 artifact bundle; it's not final Type II but shows controls and evidence we have so far.
[06:54] Samir Patel: thanks. can you also include a sample RBAC policy we can adapt?
[06:58] Priya Nair: we'll include a starter RBAC template and recommended least-privilege roles.
[07:03] Claire O'Neill: ok I'm satisfied for now - we'll triage and upload evidence as fixes land.
[07:09] Jordan Lee: great. any other questions?
[07:12] Samir Patel: one last: are you able to mask PHI/PII in logs on request? we sometimes need that for redaction.
[07:18] Priya Nair: yes - we have log redaction filters and can configure field-level redaction for specific customers.
[07:24] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the package tomorrow and set the re-test call.
[07:29] Samir Patel: thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
